stories.headline: Saudi-led forces and Houthis escalate fighting around Yemen's Bab al-Mandab strait

sources.body:
Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia say they have "secured" the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, at the start of a major offensive against the Iran-backed Houthi movement.

The Yemeni military also said in a statement that its forces had captured the Red Sea city of Mokha on Monday afternoon with the help of Saudi air strikes.

But in conflicting reports, unnamed Yemeni government and military sources later told news agencies Reuters and AFP that the forces had only reached the city's outskirts.

The Houthis denied losing Bab al-Mandab and Mokha and said they had struck Riyadh's airport and other locations in Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the air strikes.

Saudi Arabia condemned the attacks and reiterated calls for the UN Security Council's permanent members to support Yemen's internationally-recognised government.

Turkey and Pakistan, allies of Saudi Arabia, meanwhile held an emergency meeting in Riyadh and agreed to rapidly deploy military forces to Saudi Arabia in an invocation of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, according to a statement shared by Pakistan's foreign ministry.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres condemned "the continued Houthi cross-border attacks" on Saudi Arabia and said he was "deeply concerned by the sharp escalation in fighting", in a statement to AFP.

The offensive launched by the pro-government National Shield, Giants Brigades and Tihama Resistance forces in south-western Yemen on Monday reportedly saw the Houthis pushed out of most of the coastal areas they seized last month.

Four government sources told Reuters that Yemeni forces had reached the outskirts of Mokha late on Monday, and that Houthi fighters were now retreating.

Government military sources who spoke to AFP would not confirm the capture of the city, but said: "Our forces took control of the Dhubab military airfield and cut the road linking the Dhubab district to the Bab al-Mandab area."

Earlier, the Yemeni military also said its forces had seized Dhubab airport, 45km (27 miles) to the south, and were besieging Houthi fighters inside the nearby town.

Houthi‑run media cited a Houthi military source as rejecting as "Saudi propaganda" the claims that the group had lost control of Mokha, and that the group remained in control of Dhubab, Bab al‑Mandab and the Kahboub mountains near the coast.

The government said operations had also begun on other fronts on Monday, including the capital, Sanaa, which fell to the Houthis at the start of the civil war 12 years ago.

Meanwhile, a Saudi-led military coalition said its fighter jets were providing "round-the-clock" air support to the pro-government forces and had destroyed 324 "high-value" targets since the start of the offensive.

Saudi air strikes killed a schoolgirl and a woman in the Sanhan and Saawan districts of Sanaa on Monday, according to Houthi-run Al Masirah TV.

Houthi spokesman Mohammed Abdul Salam said Saudi Arabia was committing "dozens of massacres" and that it must "bear all the consequences".
sources.headline: Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway

sources.body:
Government offensive launched under air cover by Saudi military coalition aims to retake all Houthi-held territory

Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around Bab al-Mandab strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, Yemeni officials said on Monday.

The officials said forces allied with the internationally recognized government have retaken the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns.

The government push came as part of a major offensive launched early Monday under an air cover by a Saudi military coalition, aiming to retake all territory held by the Houthis .

However, the offensive came just after the rebels said they had captured more territory in the south-western part of Yemen, taking the key town of Turbah in a blow to the Saudi-backed forces as they advanced toward the strategic provincial capital of Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city.

The Saudi-led coalition spokesperson, Maj Gen Turki al-Malki, said 100 fighter jets were providing support to the forces of Yemen’s internationally recognized government fighting against the Houthis. He said the coalition had secured “air protection” of the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets as part of the ongoing campaign.

Marco Rubio told reporters that it was expected that the Saudi-backed government in Yemen would hit back at the rebels to reclaim territory. Asked if the Saudi-led coalition coordinated the action with the United States, the US secretary of state said that Saudi Arabia and the US had a defense agreement but would not offer more details.

He said the Yemeni government was ousted from some of its territory by a Houthi campaign and the Saudis had come under attack, and “they have a right to defend themselves”.

The new push sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait – a chokepoint for international shipping – after a lightning offensive by the Iran-backed Houthis.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have increasingly targeted Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, and on Sunday said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital again.

The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government’s interim capital, Aden, according to four security sources.

The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around the city.

“We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station,” a police source in the area said.

Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city. Fighting in the area was ongoing, they added.
sources.headline: Saudi-backed forces recapture key areas around strait from Houthis in Yemen

sources.body: Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on the main airport in the Saudi capital while also denying on Tuesday losing territory to government forces, as fighting intensified. After declaring a counter-offensive, government forces claimed Monday to have pushed the Houthis out of the Bab al-Mandab area, a key shipping route in the Red Sea, as well as the port city of Mocha, which was captured last month.
sources.headline: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Riyadh airport

stories.headline: French student protests spread nationwide amid clashes with police

sources.body: In Rennes, a city in north-western France, riot police can be seen using water cannon during clashes on the sidelines of a demonstration, in pictures from news agency AFP - while some people try to protect themselves with umbrellas.
sources.headline: Protesters start fires and clash with police as school demonstrations spread across France

sources.body:
Unprecedented protests that began in low-income banlieue are turning ugly, with investigations under way into police brutality

B efore dawn on Tuesday outside the Lycée Sophie-Germain in central Paris , hundreds of teenagers dragged wheelie bins, metal barriers and shopping trolleys to build a barricade outside the front door of their secondary school.

Climbing to the top of the piles of bins, pupils held banners calling for more funding and greater equality in French schools. But they were also protesting against French riot police, who have been accused by human rights groups of using disproportionate force against children in what is fast becoming the biggest youth protest movement in decades .

“Everyone hates the police,” chanted a group of 15- and 16-year-olds. At least 215 teenagers, 715 police officers and 85 teaching staff have been injured in clashes in recent days, according to the government.

“We’re teenagers with wheelie bins, and the police have heavy weapons, it’s totally mismatched,” said Livia, 17, who was studying theatre at a lycée in northern Paris and did not want her real name published. “The police are extremely violent in France . This is state violence and it’s horrible seeing police allowed to target children. It’s important to remember this is institutionalised violence, it’s planned and deliberate.”

Ten investigations into possible police brutality are under way after injuries allegedly involving the use of police weapons, including one 15-year-old who lost his hand , another who lost his eye and a boy whose jaw and teeth were shattered, leaving him, as his mother said, barely able to eat with a straw in hospital.

“The policing is catastrophic, people have been mutilated by weapons – one boy has lost an eye – it’s horrible,” said Lily, 17 (not her real name), who was studying social sciences in her final year of school and demonstrating for more funding in what she called a discriminatory education system that left poorer children behind. “My parents support me being on the barricades and at the protests. They’re worried about the policing, but they said they’d come and get me from the police station if I was arrested.”

Teenagers nearby held up cardboard signs protesting against the use of teargas and riot police. “A state that gases high school students is a weak state,” read one banner. “Gas rapists, not children,” said another sign in reference to calls for betters laws against sexual violence. Another banner read: “Not here to riot.”

The unprecedented protest movement that began outside one school in a low-income Paris suburb has spread across the country, taking the government by surprise.

Hundreds of high schools have been barricaded and forced to close as pupils protest against teacher shortages, crumbling buildings and overcrowded classes. The justice ministry said 5,060 people had been arrested ⁠since the protests began, 87% of them being minors. More than 1,800 people had been prosecuted, ​including 1,483 minors, the ministry said, without specifying ​the crimes. It said 790 cases had been ​dismissed. The government said 24 schools had been burned or ransacked.
sources.headline: On the barricades with wheelie bins and shopping trolleys: Paris students rage at politicians and police

stories.headline: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Moscow as Black Sea shipping comes under attack

sources.body: Ukraine launched overnight one of its largest drone attacks on Moscow in the past two years, killing two men and injuring several people in the Russian capital, local officials said on Tuesday.
sources.headline: Ukraine hits Moscow with one of its largest drone attacks in two years

sources.body: Bulgarian authorities on Tuesday launched a search for missing crew members of a boat that sank in its economic zone in the Black Sea after drones hit two merchant vessels. Black Sea shipping has been hit by growing fallout from the war in Ukraine in recent months.
sources.headline: Bulgaria searches for missing crew as drones hit two Black Sea ships

sources.body:
A civilian cargo ship has sunk and its crew is missing after being attacked by drones in the Black Sea, Bulgarian officials say.

A second vessel - carrying grain - was also hit within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Its 18 crew were rescued.

Radev did not say who was behind the attacks, which come as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea, particularly the eastern side, as part of its war against Ukraine.

Moscow has not commented on the latest incident, a day after it was accused by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of striking a civilian vessel carrying corn. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the attacks were "unacceptable".

Air and sea drones were involved in the attacks at about 03:00 (23:00 GMT), some 70 miles (112 km) off the coastal town of Byala in eastern Bulgaria, Radev said.

The sunken ship was flying under the flag of Togo, he said. Named the Alfa Watan, it was a Turkish-owned general cargo ship and was reportedly heading for Sulina, Romania.

Tracking data shows the ship entered the Black Sea heading north on Monday. Its last reported position on MarineTraffic was at 2343 GMT last night in the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone of the Black Sea.

It is not clear what the Alfa Watan was carrying or how many people were on board.

A Bulgarian vessel was close by, but when they arrived all they saw was an overturned boat and rafts as well as life jackets. It was not clear how many crew members were on board. A search operation has been launched. The vessel's cargo was not immediately known.

Radev said Bulgarian sailors had rescued the crew members from the second ship - including two who were injured in a fire on board. Eleven were Turkish and seven Indian nationals. That ship, the Able, was flying the flag of Palau and transporting grain.

Its last reported position was five nautical miles (9km) from the Alfa Watan.

Radev condemned the strikes as "a flagrant violation of maritime law".

He told reporters: "Such an attack within the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone is absolutely unacceptable."

He did not accuse Russia of carrying out the strikes, but referred to the war in Ukraine, saying: "As I have long maintained, if this war is not halted in time, it will continue to expand its geographical reach and increase risks, including the risk of a global conflict."

European Commission President von der Leyen wrote on X: "The situation in the Black Sea is increasingly concerning.

"Commercial ships – and innocent crews – are being targeted, with lives already lost at sea," she said. "While exact circumstances of these incidents are still being established, the developments are very concerning."

"Attacks on civilian shipping are unacceptable."

The government said it would convene an emergency meeting on Tuesday to discuss the strikes.

Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea is just over 29,000 sq km (11,197 sq miles), about 6% of the total size of the Black Sea.

A separate attack on Tuesday, near Odesa, saw a crew member killed and seven more injured. The ship was flying the flag of the Marshall Islands, according to Ukrainian media.
sources.headline: Ship sinks and crew missing after Black Sea drone attack

stories.headline: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as the outbreak spreads from DR Congo

sources.body:
Kenya has confirmed its first ever case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.

Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago, and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in Nairobi.

Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died. However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.

Since then, all known cases of the highly infectious disease have been in DR Congo.

The virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment.

​​There are however four vaccines in development, with human trials for one of them being launched in July.

Duale confirmed that the Kenyan national had tested positive for the Bundibugyo species.

According to the minister, the patient first travelled by road from DR Congo to the Ugandan capital Kampala, where he boarded a flight to Nairobi.

Duale said that after being taken to the Nairobi Hospital, the patient was transferred to an isolation facility which was built during the Covid-19 pandemic.

It was there that the patient "developed fever, chills, intense fatigue and weakness, painful swallowing, muscle pain and bleeding under the skin".

"Doctors suspected a viral haemorrhagic fever based on his symptoms and travel history and collected samples for testing. The sample tested positive for Ebola Bundibugyo virus," Duale said.

The patient died at 23:30 (20:30 GMT) on Monday and his burial is planned for later on Tuesday in line with public health safety protocols.

At least 28 contacts, including family members and healthcare workers, have been identified, while health authorities are tracing a further 23 passengers and four crew members who travelled on the same flight.

The health minister has urged Kenyans "not to panic, as all systems are in place to mitigate the spread of the disease".

He asked health workers to be "extra vigilant and maintain the highest infection prevention and control measures regardless of the condition being treated".

The WHO has recorded 4,082 deaths out of 8,463 cases in the current outbreak, making it the largest ever recorded in DR Congo, where Ebola was first discovered.

Medical charity MSF believes the current toll could be even higher because of gaps in surveillance and testing in the war-torn country.

On Monday, MSF said the virus was spreading "like a megafire", with new hotspots emerging in North Kivu province, which borders Ituri where the virus began.
sources.headline: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads

sources.body:
Health minister says 28 contacts identified after death of citizen who arrived from DRC on Saturday

Kenya has reported its first-ever Ebola death, the health minister announced on Tuesday, after a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) died after returning to the country.

In mid-May, the DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak, an extremely deadly disease that has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.

While Kenya has previously never reported a case, neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 Ebola cases – almost all people who had travelled from the DRC – and two deaths, before being declared Ebola-free in August.

The Kenyan citizen, who has not been named, fell ill about a month ago and had been treated in the DRC, Aden Duale, the Kenyan health minister, told reporters, before travelling overland to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, and then flying to Nairobi on 3 October.

Duale said the man was suffering “fever, chills, intense fatigue, weakness, muscle pain, painful swallowing, sore throat and bleeding under the skin at the injection sites”.

He said the man was subsequently screened and confirmed positive for the virus, saying that he “regrettably passed on last night at around 1130” in the evening (2030 GMT).

Duale said officials had listed 28 contacts of the deceased, including family members and healthcare workers, but that so far “only one test has turned positive and is the one that we have just discussed”.

However, he added that authorities were pursuing a further 23 passengers and four crew members who were on the same flight with the man and that “arrangements” for quarantine for those at risk had been prepared. “I wish to assure the public not to panic, as all systems are in place to mitigate the spread of the disease,” he said.

Duale said that arrangements for a “safe and dignified burial” of the man were planned for later in the day in line with public health standards. He did not disclose further details.

As of 2 October, the World Health Organization had recorded 4,082 deaths out of 8,463 cases since the emergence in the DRC of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment.

After starting in the north-eastern Ituri province, the current outbreak has spread to seven provinces in the north and east.

The virus has hit unstable regions in the vast central African country where armed clashes and violence, alongside a critical lack of resources, have hindered the health response.

The medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières warned on Monday of an “alarming surge” in cases in eastern North Kivu province, which borders Uganda.

Kenyans reacted furiously to government plans earlier this year for the creation of an Ebola facility at Laikipia airbase, about 125 miles from Nairobi.
sources.headline: Kenya confirms first Ebola case as virus ‘surges’ in DR Congo province

stories.headline: Quebec separatists win election, promising a 2029 independence referendum

sources.body:
Canada's Parti Québécois (PQ) is projected to have won enough seats in Quebec's provincial election to form a minority government, though the separatists will need other parties' support to achieve their aims - such as a new public vote on independence.

It marks the first time the PQ has been in power since 2014, with Paul St-Pierre Plamondon set to become the province's new leader.

In his victory speech, St-Pierre Plamondon again raised his independence plans but vowed to be "the premier of everyone in Quebec".

The result could prove a fresh test for Prime Minister Mark Carney, also setting up confrontations with Québec over issues like immigration and the monarchy.

In its effort to achieve independence, the PQ has pledged to hold a referendum on separating from the rest of Canada.

The majority French-speaking province has held other votes on this, in 1980 and 1995. On both occasions, the independence movement was defeated. Polls indicate only about 30% of Quebecers back such a move this time.

St-Pierre Plamondon has previously said the vote would occur after President Donald Trump is out of office south of the border in the United States, explaining that would require "conditions that allow for an informed and serene debate". The US and Canada are in a trade war as a result of Trump's programme of tariffs.

In his victory speech after Monday's election results, St-Pierre Plamondon said of the potential referendum: "Our national destiny will be achieved one day."

But it is not clear how the PQ leader would secure the vote that he wants - given that rival parties, upon whose support he would depend, oppose independence.

Quebec Liberal Leader Charles Milliard said his party is prepared to support the PQ on a number of issues, but "there is no way we will collaborate on a potential referendum".

Despite winning the most amount of seats of any party, the PQ's share of the popular vote is only 28%.

With most votes counted on Tuesday morning, the party was set to win fewer than the 64 seats needed to command a majority in the province's assembly, according to projections from Canadian media.

The Liberals - the provincial party with links to Carney's federal Liberals - are projected to have increased their number of seats in the assembly, as have the Conservatives.

All parties benefited from the collapse of the Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ), which was previously the province's governing party but is not projected to have won a single seat this time.

Carney congratulated Plamondon, saying he looked forward to working with the new provincial leader, adding: "Building a stronger Quebec is at the heart of our mission to build a stronger Canada."

Carney may find himself managing dual unity crises in different parts of the country, depending on the outcome of a vote in Alberta on whether to have a referendum of its own.

Trump is due to leave office in just over two years, meaning that if Plamondon is able to enact his pledge, a third vote on independence would likely be scheduled for 2029 or 2030.
sources.headline: Separatist party projected to win Quebec election, adding new test to Canada's unity

sources.body:
Parti Québécois promises to hold independence referendum in Canada’s French-speaking region by 2028

Voters in Quebec are going to the polls in provincial elections which will probably result in victory for a party that has promised to hold a referendum on independence from Canada within the next two years.

If polls are correct, the Parti Québécois (PQ) will form the government of the province of roughly nine million, the first time that the separatist movement will have gained power in the French-speaking region for more than a decade.

A PQ victory in Monday’s election would also be likely to trigger a return to pitched battles over questions of language and identity between Quebec and the federal government.

Long considered a declining force in Quebec politics , the PQ owes its resurgence to party leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon. The 49-year-old Oxford-educated lawyer and polyglot has positioned himself as a TikToking gen-X rebuttal to François Legault, Quebec’s long-serving Premier until he resigned early this year.

Analysts say that St-Pierre Plamondon’s electoral success is not because he is a separatist – the majority of voters do not support an independent Quebec – but because of his rightwing take on red-meat identity issues.

He has blamed immigrants for Quebec’s overflowing schools, increased crime and skyrocketing housing prices, while promising to slash immigration levels and ban “conspicuous” religious symbols from the bodies of teachers and their students. He has derided his critics from the leftist Quebec Solidaire party as “woke”, and has taken to repeating the talking points of hard-right columnists.

Many in the province agree with St-Pierre Plamondon’s rhetoric, even though it strays from PQ’s social democratic roots, according to radio host Patrick Lagacé. “Most Quebecers traditionally see themselves as being on the left. Increasingly, though, they are on the right when it comes to social issues like systemic racism and accommodation of religious behaviour. They’ve hardened on these issues, and don’t see themselves in the left’s recent fixation on identity issues,” Lagacé said.

The biggest drag on St-Pierre Plamondon’s popularity has been his oft-repeated promise to hold a referendum during the first mandate of a PQ government. An overwhelming majority of Quebecers don’t want such a thing any time soon – particularly with Canada locked in a trade war with the US. The province mostly voted for Liberal leader Mark Carney over the separatist Bloc Québécois in last year’s federal election, expressly because of Carney’s “elbows up” posturing against the Trump administration.

But for the PQ, Donald Trump was at first a curse , then a gift. Early in the campaign, St-Pierre Plamondon said he wouldn’t hold a referendum as long as Trump was in power, defusing the issue and allowing St-Pierre Plamondon to concentrate on attacking immigration and immigrants.

The party has also benefited from a four-way race for the right-leaning nationalist vote beyond the reliably Liberal fiefdom of Montreal – particularly around Quebec city, where the upstart Parti Conservateur du Québec has made significant inroads. “The Parti Québécois is benefiting from a massive vote split because those who don’t like the PQ don’t agree on who to vote for,” said poll analyst Philippe Fournier.
sources.headline: Quebec poised to elect separatists to power for first time in more than a decade

stories.headline: Germany arrests former intelligence chief on espionage and treason allegations

sources.body:
Former German spy chief August Hanning has been arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, the German Federal Prosecutor's Office says.

Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.

Prosecutors allege that he used classified intelligence to "draft an analysis" for one foreign intelligence service and maintained contact with another foreign spying service. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.

Police also arrested former BND employee Mandred D, accusing him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents for money.

Manfred D, who was Hanning's bureau chief and remained in the BND until this year, is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.

Local media reported Hanning was arrested at his home in Nordwalde near Münster while Manfred D was arrested in Bavaria. Hanning is due in court on Wednesday and Manfred D will appear on Tuesday.

Prosecutors say Mandred D, who also served as the chief of staff for Hanning's successors between 2012 and 2026, used his role to gain access to highly confidential information which he then passed on to Hanning "in exchange for remuneration".

"The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the Federal Intelligence Service for internal purposes," the statement says.

"On one occasion, Hanning used classified intelligence ... to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service," prosecutors said, noting it was not clear if "the material reached the intended recipient".

Hanning is also accused of being "in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D, for several years".

Local media say Hanning's alleged possession of intelligence documents came to light during a separate case relating to German steakhouse heiress Christina Block.

Hamburg public prosecutor's office accused Block of orchestrating the kidnapping of her two youngest children in 2023 due to a custody dispute. Investigators allege Hanning was involved in an earlier attempted kidnapping of the children, which he denies.

State criminal police officers reportedly discovered an electronic data storage device containing sensitive information including recent BND documents.

It is not the first time the BND has faced similar controversy. A high-ranking German intelligence officer was charged with treason in 2023 for allegedly passing state secrets to Russia.

Prosecutors alleged Carsten L shared intelligence about the war in Ukraine and the Wagner mercenary group and received roughly €400,000 ($450,000; £340,000). His trial is ongoing.
sources.headline: Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason

sources.body:
August Hanning served as president of federal intelligence service from 1998 to 2005

A former head of Germany’s foreign intelligence service has been arrested on suspicion of treason and spying on behalf of an overseas intelligence agency, prosecutors said.

August Hanning, 80, was head of the federal intelligence service (BND) – which operates outside Germany to gather information across the fields of political, economic, and military intelligence – between 1998 and 2005.

He was arrested at his home in Nordwalde near Münster early on Tuesday. His former chief of staff, identified only as Manfred D, was arrested at the same time in Bavaria, on suspicion of “aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage”, according to a prosecutor’s statement. Media pictures showed Hanning, dressed in an open-necked white shirt, being taken from his redbrick house to a bullet-proof vehicle by masked officers.

Manfred D, who continued to work for Hanning’s successors at the BND after Hanning’s departure until the present day, is accused of using his role to gain access to classified information which he then handed to Hanning “in exchange for payment”, the prosecutors’ statement continued.

“The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the federal intelligence service for internal purposes, particularly for executive intelligence briefings,” the statement said.

Prosecutors believe that Hanning intended to resell the documents as part of a paid consulting role he had built up after leaving the BND, prosecutors added. To what extent and to whom he disseminated them remains part of an ongoing investigation.

He is accused of using the information to “draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service”, prosecutors said. It was unclear if this information had reached its intended recipient, they added.

Over several years Hanning is also believed to have passed on potentially sensitive political information, in part based on information passed to him by Manfred D, to a close contact representing a separate foreign intelligence service.

Several properties connected to both men were being searched simultaneously on Tuesday, including in Berlin.

Manfred D is due to appear before judges at the federal court of justice in Karlsruhe later on Tuesday, while Hanning is scheduled to appear on Wednesday.

Suspicions over Hanning’s activities emerged as a result of an investigation into the kidnappings of the children from a prominent Hamburg business family, which is the focus of a major trial in the north German port city.

Investigators were led to Hanning over allegations, which he denies, that he helped Christina Block, heiress of a steak restaurant dynasty, to organise the violent cross-border seizure in Denmark of her children from her estranged husband who has custody of two of their children. Block denies the charges.
sources.headline: Germany arrests former intelligence chief over alleged spying

stories.headline: Francis Halzen wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for cosmic-neutrino research

sources.body:
Belgian physicist Prof Francis Halzen has won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his pioneering work on an observatory that detects particles from space, shedding light on the distant universe.

Halzen led the development of IceCube at the South Pole, which uses a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice fitted with light sensors to detect particles called neutrinos. These carry information about violent, high-energy processes in the cosmos.

The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said "his vision and scientific leadership have been fundamental for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory".

Halzen first presented his vision for detecting neutrinos at the South Pole in 1988.

He told a news conference that he was surprised his idea worked so well.

"I have to emphasise how lucky I was. Because when we started this project, everybody realised this was maybe a good idea, but very few thought it would work, including myself."

Neutrinos are elusive subatomic particles. The Sun produces vast numbers of them: every second, billions pass harmlessly through an area the size of your fingernail.

But IceCube is searching for much higher-energy neutrinos, those produced by violent processes far beyond our Solar System — in distant galaxies.

It is composed of thousands of sensors on long cables that are drilled and frozen into a 1km cubic block of ice.

Neutrinos can be thought of as astronomical messengers that point to those fundamental events.

At the observatory, most neutrinos pass straight through the ice, but occasionally one interacts with it, producing particles that give off a telltale flash of light.

These rare signals carry clues to where the neutrinos came from and the extreme conditions that produced them — allowing scientists to investigate places that ordinary telescopes cannot easily see.

"Francis Halzen has led an international team of researchers and engineers who have provided us with a fantastic instrument," said Prof Mark Pearce, Chair of the Nobel Committee for Physics.

"His tenacity and scientific vision has paved the way for a new kind of astronomy."

On the rare occasions when a neutrino strikes an atomic nucleus, it produces fast-moving charged particles. It is these racing through the ice, which give off a blue glow, which sensitive light detectors can pick up.

The pattern and timing of that light allow scientists to estimate the direction the neutrino came from — helping them trace its origins in the cosmos. But these interactions are so rare that the observatory needed an enormous volume of clear ice.

Halzen's idea was to use a vast natural ice sheet in Antarctica. So began an audacious plan to build a neutrino observatory at the geographic South Pole, with thousands of light sensors embedded deep in the ice.

The neutrino's ghostly nature, the very thing that makes it so hard to detect, also makes it a powerful messenger from the distant Universe.

Neutrinos rarely interact with material in its way, so they can go right through dense regions that light cannot easily penetrate.

And because they have no electric charge, magnetic fields do not bend their paths through space. That means their direction of arrival can point scientists back towards their source.
sources.headline: 'Ghost particles' from space telescope wins physics Nobel

sources.body:
Tres miembros de la Academia Sueca anuncian el premio a Francis Halzen 

El descubrimiento de neutrinos de alta energía de origen cósmico ha sido galardonado con el premio Nobel de Física de 2026. El galardón se ha concedido a Francis Halzen, científico nacido en Bélgica que ha sido profesor de la Universidad de Wisconsin-Madison en EE.UU. desde 1972.

Ha sido premiado “por sus contribuciones decisivas al Observatorio de Neutrinos IceCube y al descubrimiento de neutrinos de alta energía de origen astrofísico”, según el veredicto de la Real Academia de Ciencias Sueca, que otorga el galardón.

Los neutrinos son partículas extremadamente abundantes en el Universo que tienen la asombrosa propiedad de atravesar la materia sin interactuar con ella. Cada segundo unos cien billones de neutrinos procedentes del Sol pasan a través de nuestro cuerpo sin llegar a tocarnos. Como apenas tienen masa, son insensibles a la fuerza de la gravedad. También son insensibles al electromagnetismo, por lo que apenas interaccionan con los átomos. De ahí que, pese a ser tan abundantes, sean indetectables con telescopios convencionales y que la información que pueden aportar sobre su origen no pueda ser leída.

“Francis Halzen se dio cuenta de que el hielo del polo sur se podía utilizar para rastrear neutrinos”, señala la Academia Nobel en el comunicado en que anuncia el premio. “Su visión y liderazgo científico han sido fundamentales para el Observatorio de Neutrinos IceCube -un kilómetro cúbico de hielo equipado con sensores-”.

Halzen presentó su idea para detectar neutrinos en la Antártida en 1988. Argumentó que, en los rarísimos casos en que un neutrino interactúa con un átomo, emite un tipo particular de radiación (la radiación de Cherenkov) que se puede observar con sensores colocados en el hielo. Le costó 23 años convencer a la comunidad científica, conseguir la financiación y construir el observatorio. Pero en 2011 el IceCube estaba por fin terminado y a punto para entrar en servicio.

Poco después detectó sus primeros neutrinos de alta energía y se pudo demostrar que no venían del Sol sino de fuera del sistema solar. “La búsqueda de las fuentes de neutrinos del universo pudo empezar en serio”, destaca la Academia Sueca en su comunicado.

Los astrofísicos saben desde hace décadas que el Universo está lleno de aceleradores de partículas naturales, que emiten partículas con energías mucho más altas que las que se consiguen en los aceleradores de la Tierra. Pero “mucho de estas fuentes es un misterio: ¿qué son?, ¿dónde están?, ¿y cuáles son los fenómenos principales que se producen en su interior?”, añade la Academia.

“Francis Halzen ha liderado un equipo internacional de científicos e ingenieros que nos han proporcionado un instrumento fantástico. Su tenacidad y visión científica ha abierto la vía a un nuevo tipo de astronomía”, ha declarado Mark Pearce, presidente del Comité Nobel de Física.

Siguiendo la tradición, el Nobel de Física es el segundo que se hace público. Cada premio, que se otorga a un máximo de tres investigadores en cada disciplina, está dotado este año con 12 millones de coronas suecas (1,06 millones de euros). Ayer se concedió el de Medicina  a al estaodunidense Karl Deisseroth y a los alemanes Peter Hegemann y Georg Nagel por el desarrollo de la optogenética, una técnica que permite controlar las neuronas con luz y que ha abierto una nueva era en el estudio del cerebro.

stories.headline: Trump approves firing-squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan

sources.body:
The Pentagon has announced it will execute a former US Army major by firing squad, the first such military execution in more than 60 years.

Nidal Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced on social media on Monday that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth had made the recommendation and President Donald Trump approved it.

It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.

Parnell said the secretary of the US Army would set the time and place of the execution.

"Judgement day for Hasan has finally come," he wrote on X.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, killed 13 soldiers at the base in Texas in 2009 and later admitted in court he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes".

He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

The attack took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

Hasan is currently one of four inmates on the US military's death row.

A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law.

It also requires appellate review and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.

The US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces deemed the military death penalty unconstitutional in 1983 but it was reinstated the following year by an executive order under then-President Ronald Reagan.

Military executions differ from those carried out at the state level.

The majority of executions in the US are carried out on the state level, with 27 states, the military and the federal government still having capital punishment as a legally available option.

Death by firing squad is rather uncommon. There was an execution by firing squad carried out last year in South Carolina, a first for the state and the first time the method was used in the US in 15 years.

Four other states allow the use of a firing squad, including Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Utah.

Trump has been a proponent of the federal death penalty and re-instated it through an executive order on the first day of his administration in January 2025.

Under his predecessor, former President Joe Biden, the justice department had issued a moratorium on the federal use of the death penalty.

The executive order signed by Trump describes capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens".

sources.body:
Nidal Hasan, convicted of killing 13 at Fort Hood, to face execution under rare military order.

United States President Donald Trump has ordered the use of a firing squad in the execution of a former army psychiatrist who killed 13 people in a mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, the Pentagon spokesman has said.

Nidal Hasan, a US citizen of Palestinian descent, would be the first US soldier to be executed by the US military in more than 60 years.

Hasan will be killed by a firing squad under the recommendation of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the approval of the president, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement on X on Monday.

The Army secretary will decide a time and place for the execution, he said.

“Judgement day for Hasan has finally come,” Parnell wrote.

Hasan was sentenced to death in August 2013 after a military jury found him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted murder for shooting a handgun in a medical facility at the Texas military base.

The attack killed 12 unarmed active-duty soldiers and a retired serviceman, and wounded 32 others.

Police arrested him at the scene, where he was shot and left partially paralysed.

The shooting took place weeks before Hasan was set to be deployed to Afghanistan.

He said during his court-martial that the shooting was an effort to stop the soldiers from going to Afghanistan and killing his fellow Muslims, and made almost no effort to defend himself.

The Trump administration added death by firing squad as an appropriate method of execution in April, along with gas asphyxiation and electrocution.

Military executions are extremely rare in the US and can only be approved by the president under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. If the order is carried out, he will be the first member of the US military to be executed since 1961.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, the 1961 execution was carried out by hanging. The apparent last known execution by a US military firing squad was one carried out “by musketry” in November 1945, the center reported.

stories.headline: AI-safety advocates demand stronger limits on OpenAI-linked political spending

sources.body: AI safety groups aren't buying OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s shifting stance on political spending in the midterms. They’re wary of his concession that campaign cash from industry-aligned groups, like the OpenAI-aligned Leading the Future super PAC, may have inadvertently backfired. Instead, they’re pushing for stronger commitments to downsize the flood of money — and for candidates to reject any support from pro-AI groups. “I won’t believe that they are actually changing their strategy, or their goals I should say, unless and until they do,” said Democratic New York assemblymember Alex Bores, who emerged as a key voice among AI regulation advocates after Leading the Future and other groups spent $8 million to tank his House campaign. He launched a $30 million effort to unify Democrats on AI policy last month. Altman’s stark acknowledgement to POLITICO follows a New York Times report that revealed OpenAI President Greg Brockman backed out of injecting more cash into Leading the Future earlier this summer, calling the super PAC’s efforts a “distraction” from the company’s mission. The pause is notable as Americans grow increasingly anxious about the risks the technology poses, and lawmakers scramble to figure out how to approach the emerging tech. Still, some critics are not taking Altman’s concession or Brockman’s pullback as a sign of a fundamental change in the industry’s campaign strategy — at least not yet. “What I read it as is they are no longer — or Greg Brockman in particular is not — going to fund Leading the Future,” said Bores. “Does that mean that the industry is not going to spend hundreds of millions of dollars trying to influence policy and get benefits on their way? No.” Bores insisted that candidates should think twice before accepting financial support from Leading the Future specifically: “An elected official of either party taking money from Leading the Future should be viewed with incredible suspect.” Guardrails Alliance political director Charlie Blaettler agreed, saying OpenAI leadership deciding to distance themselves from Leading the Future should be the final straw for Democrats backed by the group. “If it’s too toxic for Sam Altman and Greg Brockman, why are Democrats still taking their money?” he said. Leading the Future and rival super PAC network Public First — which advocates for AI regulation and is largely funded by OpenAI competitor Anthropic — together spent over $70 million through super PACs this cycle, according to FEC data. Other pro-regulation advocates have jumped in with their own political spending, with groups like the Guardrails Alliance — a nonprofit and super PAC that launched in June — raising $5 million and spending hundreds of thousands of dollars to support Bores. Some of Guardrails Alliance’s money came from OpenAI employees pushing back against Leading the Future, which is funded in large part by OpenAI president Brockman, his wife Anna, early OpenAI investors Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, and their venture capital firm a16z. They have contributed a combined $75 million to Leading the Future. Leading the Future and a16z declined to comment. Some Democrats who were backed in their primaries by Leading the Future — like Reps. Ritchie Torres and Joe Morelle of New York and Jared Moskowitz of Florida — declined to say whether they would disavow the Leading the Future cash that boosted them in their races. “An outside AI PAC spent money in the 4th district during the primary, but they didn’t donate directly to my campaign,” Rep. Val Hoyle (D-Ore.), who was backed by a nearly $300,000 investment from Leading the Future, said in a statement to POLITICO. She did not address whether she would disavow the group and its spending: “I’ve been working with labor leaders and advocates to put workers first when it comes to AI. We need clear federal guardrails to protect workers, safeguard our planet, prevent utility rate spikes and give consumers a voice.” Even if candidates decide to further distance themselves from the industry’s spending, some pro-guardrails advocates said the onus still lies with figures like Altman to put a stop to — or significantly decrease — the influx of money altogether. “[Altman was] basically saying, ‘These are the rules of the game, and I can’t really change them, and it’s not in my job description,’” said Brendan Steinhauser, who leads AI safety group The Alliance for Secure AI Action. “Of course he’s saying that, but they could do a unilateral disarmament or encourage the other labs to stop giving, and maybe it’d be just like pacing the frontier — maybe people could pace political giving.” Former Democratic Rep. Brad Carson, who co-founded Public First, said he would be open to engaging in talks with Leading the Future about pacing or scaling back the industry’s political spending — but only if so-called AI “accelerationists” are serious about backing off. He called out Andreessen and Horowitz who have emerged as the biggest known spenders in this year’s midterm elections and were early investors in OpenAI. “As long as these accelerationists have a desire to spend tens and tens, if not hundreds of millions of dollars, there is probably a need for a Public First,” said Carson, who also leads the nonprofit group Americans for Responsible Innovation. “So even if Brockman drops out, Andreessen and Horowitz can just drop another 50 million if they felt like it, and I wouldn’t want to be disarmed against that.” Brendan Bordelon contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Spain's Constitutional Court clears the way for Carles Puigdemont's return

sources.body: <p>El Pleno del Tribunal Constitucional ha dictado que el Supremo debe amnistiar la malversación que los políticos catalanes cometieron en el contexto del proceso independentista, según la sentencia aprobada este martes por la mayoría progresista y de la que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-28/el-presidente-del-constitucional-defiende-amnistiar-la-malversacion-del-proces-es-lo-unico-conciliable-con-la-logica-y-el-sentido-comun.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-28/el-presidente-del-constitucional-defiende-amnistiar-la-malversacion-del-proces-es-lo-unico-conciliable-con-la-logica-y-el-sentido-comun.html">ha sido ponente el presidente del tribunal de garantías, Cándido Conde-Pumpido</a>. La sentencia declara que, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-07-01/el-supremo-rechaza-amnistiar-la-malversacion-en-el-proces-y-mantiene-la-orden-de-detencion-a-puigdemont.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-07-01/el-supremo-rechaza-amnistiar-la-malversacion-en-el-proces-y-mantiene-la-orden-de-detencion-a-puigdemont.html">al denegar a la exconsejera de Trabajo Dolors Bassa la aplicación de la amnistía</a> por ese delito, la Sala de lo Penal del Supremo vulneró su derecho a la tutela judicial efectiva con una “interpretación extensiva, contraria al espíritu y finalidad de la norma” y “contradictoria” de la ley de amnistía. Y, en consecuencia, considera que lo que procede es que el Supremo “dicte una nueva resolución en la que se declare amnistiado el delito de malversación de caudales públicos por el que fue condenada”. Esta doctrina, que se aplica también al caso del expresidente de la Generalitat Carles Puigdemont y da vía libre para su regreso después de que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/el-supremo-levanta-la-orden-de-detencion-a-puigdemont.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/el-supremo-levanta-la-orden-de-detencion-a-puigdemont.html">el Supremo haya levantado la orden de detención activada contra él</a>. La aplicación de la amnistía permitirá, a su vez, que los líderes del <i>procés </i>condenados y procesados puedan volver a presentarse a unas elecciones. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/via-libre-al-regreso-de-puigdemont-el-constitucional-ordena-al-supremo-que-amnistie-la-malversacion-del-proces.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El Constitucional ordena al Supremo que amnistíe la malversación del ‘procés’

sources.body: <p>Carles Puigdemont ya puede volver a España sin riesgo de ser detenido. El magistrado del Tribunal Supremo Pablo Llarena ha levantado la orden de detención nacional que pesaba sobre el expresidente catalán y los exconsejeros Toni Comín y Lluís Puig desde octubre de 2017, cuando salieron de España rumbo a Bélgica horas antes de que la Fiscalía se querellara por rebelión contra ellos y el resto del Govern. Llarena ha tomado esta decisión minutos después de que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/via-libre-al-regreso-de-puigdemont-el-constitucional-ordena-al-supremo-que-amnistie-la-malversacion-del-proces.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/via-libre-al-regreso-de-puigdemont-el-constitucional-ordena-al-supremo-que-amnistie-la-malversacion-del-proces.html">el Tribunal Constitucional diera la razón a los exdirigentes independentistas</a> y declarara que el Supremo debió aplicarles en 2024 la ley de amnistía por el delito de malversación, el único por el que aún estaban procesados. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/el-supremo-levanta-la-orden-de-detencion-a-puigdemont.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El Supremo levanta la orden de detención a Puigdemont

sources.body:
El Tribunal Constitucional ordena al Tribunal Supremo que aplique la amnistía a los líderes del procés procesados o condenados por el delito de malversación de caudales públicos. El tribunal de garantías acaba de aprobar con la mayoría progresista de 7 votos a favor frente a 5 en contra la ponencia de su presidente, Cándido Conde-Pumpido, que estima que el alto tribunal vulneró tres artículos de la Constitución al negarse a amnistiar a los encausados por el procés, según confirman a La Vanguardia fuentes del tribunal.

La sentencia, que cuenta con votos particulares de la minoría conservadora, resuelve el recurso de la exconsellera Dolors Bassa aunque en la práctica se hace extensible al resto de los máximos responsables del Govern en el 2017. Ahora el Supremo deberá acatar la sentencia, anular el auto por el que se negaba llevar a cabo la amnistía y acordar su aplicación.

En el Pleno de hoy, también se estudiaba la ponencia del conservador José María Macías respecto del recurso del exconseller Jordi Turull. Aunque en la sesión anterior anunció que se quedaba con la ponencia para incorporar el criterio de la mayoría conservadora, finalmente hoy ha optado por renunciar a ella. La ha asumido el propio Conde-Pumpido, que la rehará con la misma doctrina que la fijada ya en la sentencia de Bassa.

Esta historia tiene dos nombres propios; el expresidente Carles Puigdemont y el vicepresidente Oriol Junqueras. Ambos, nueve años después del procés, siguen liderando sus partidos. El primero lleva todo este tiempo en Bélgica, huído para evitar ser enjuiciado y encarcelado en España al igual que sus compañeros de partido. Sus movimientos políticos han permitido que ahora pueda volver sin ser juzgado.

Con la sentencia de hoy, el único paso que le queda es que el juez isntructor Pablo Llarena aplique la amnistía, levante la orden de detención nacional que pesa sobre él y archive la causa que tiene abierta.

Una vez que el magistrado cumpla con la orden del Constitucional, Puigdemont podrá volver a Catalunya, probablemente coincidiendo con la campaña electoral para las generales que anunció ayer el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, para el próximo 29 de noviembre.

Lo que no parece que tendrá será una fotografía con Pedro Sánchez en La Moncloa. Su partido, Junts, ha sido uno de los responsables de que no hayan salido adelante los decretos sobre la vivienda votados la semana pasada en el Congreso de los Diputados y lo que ha llevado a Sánchez a convocar elecciones.

Después de los votos en contra de los posconvergentes , lo único que le queda al Ejecutivo es defender que la Amnistía fue necesaria para la normalización de Catalunya. Para lanzar este mensaje, los socialistas se acogerán a la sentencia dictada el pasado mes de julio por el Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea (TJUE) que certificó que la ley del olvidó sirvió para la “reconciliación”.

El otro nombre es el de Oriol Junqueras. En su caso sí fue juzgado y condenado por un delito de sedición y malversación. Fue encarcelado aunque salió antes de tiempo después de que el Gobierno le indultara. Aún así todavía tiene la pena de 13 años de inhabilitación y por eso busca la amnistía. En cuanto el Supremo archive las consencuencias penales de la condena, Junqueras puede volver a prensentarse como candidato por ERC.

stories.headline: Spain's parties begin campaigning after Sánchez calls a November 29 general election

sources.body:
Pedro Sánchez no agotará la legislatura, pese a haberlo repetido numerosas veces en los últimos años. Este lunes convocó las elecciones generales para el primer día que es legalmente posible, el 29 de noviembre, y con ello dio el pistoletazo de salida a un calendario que obliga a todas las formaciones políticas a encender su maquinaria electoral , casi en un tiempo récord, revolucionando así el tablero político.

El presidente del Gobierno se dirigió directamente a la ciudadanía a primera hora de la mañana tras un fin de semana de reflexión por el fracaso de sus decretos en vivienda, que terminó de incendiar las protestas en la calle que comenzaron con el desahucio de Maricarmen: "Ha llegado el momento de que decidáis qué futuro queréis ". Al respecto, plantea elegir entre dos disyuntivas: "La ola ultraderechista que involuciona" o que España siga siendo "baluarte de apertura y justicia social y responsabilidad medioambiental".

Los hay más y menos preparados para la cita electoral. En la derecha llevaban años, prácticamente desde el inicio de la legislatura, exigiendo elecciones anticipadas por una legislatura, como decían en el PP, que "nunca debió existir".

Los 'populares' ya tuvieron su congreso nacional el año pasado para rearmar su estrategia frente a Sánchez y dar la cara en unas elecciones que, con todo, pensaban que llegarían antes dados los casos de corrupción que cercaban al partido y al Gobierno. Alberto Núñez Feijóo salió reforzado como líder con un partido cohesionado que sigue el primero en todas las encuestas, que le otorgan una victoria inapelable, aunque todavía necesitaría a Vox para gobernar.

En ese momento, se comprometió a gobernar en solitario y no en coalición con Vox y lo recalcó para que quedara en la hemeroteca. Desde entonces, ha ido matizando sus afirmaciones diciendo que su deseo es un gobierno monocolor pero que dependerá de lo que digan los ciudadanos con su voto.

Feijóo ha celebrado que "por fin" España va a tener elecciones y también ha llamado a los ciudadanos a e legir entre "corrupción o decencia, decadencia o prosperidad ": "La pregunta que propongo a los ciudadanos es si quieren cuatro años más de lo que estamos viviendo o dar oportunidad al cambio". Y tanto él como todo su partido están lanzando la idea de que España necesita "una reconstrucción nacional".

Los de Santiago Abascal también pisan con fuerza en los sondeos y serán, previsiblemente, quienes tengan la llave de un futuro Gobierno, como ha ocurrido en territorios como Extremadura, Aragón, Castilla y León y Andalucía en las últimas elecciones autonómicas.

Abascal ha celebrado igualmente la "excelente noticia" de que haya unas elecciones, pero ha sembrado la duda sobre el proceso electoral en caso de que Sánchez lo "manipule" porque "es capaz de todo". Con todo, ha añadido: " Estamos preparados para ofrecer a los españoles la alternativa que necesitan".

Está por ver si el líder de Vox exige ser vicepresidente y tener algún ministerio o le basta con un acuerdo de investidura o también posiblemente de gobierno.

Rodeada de activistas del Sindicato de Inquilinas, de caras conocidas y muy identificadas con el progresismo —como Ana Belén, Juan Diego Botto y Carlos Bardem—, Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 años, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-23/maricarmen-se-queda-un-centenar-de-activistas-espera-junto-a-la-anciana-a-la-comision-judicial.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-23/maricarmen-se-queda-un-centenar-de-activistas-espera-junto-a-la-anciana-a-la-comision-judicial.html">abandonaba su casa en camilla,</a> desahuciada por el fondo que la compró, después de 70 años pagando su alquiler. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-06/asi-gesto-sanchez-el-adelanto-electoral-este-congreso-no-nos-vale-tenemos-que-ir-a-elecciones-podemos-ganar.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/W3ZCY2HR6RAENBJJUZ4VUT66JI.JPG?auth=036ce9b94d2f4c8f3cfe2da9a04ec43c0a0ed5aada69458e6465c58bcc969c28" width="3744" height="2496" alt="La portavoz de Junts en el Congreso, Miriam Nogueras, el 2 de octubre."></img>

L'anunci d' eleccions de Pedro Sánchez no ha arribat per sorpresa i, quan divendres va anunciar que s'agafava uns dies per reflexionar, la majoria dels partits ja intuïen que seria per convocar els comicis.

Així mateix, ha afegit que "més que mai, Catalunya està amb Pedro Sánchez ".

Un Govern que va néixer per avançar no pot aturar-se perquè alguns prefereixin el bloqueig. Que ningú s'equivoqui: si hi ha eleccions, és el moment de decidir entre continuar avançant o tornar enrere. Catalunya no es resigna. Catalunya no es rendeix. Catalunya estarà amb Pedro @sanchezcastejon. Ara, més que mai.

Després d'haver-l'hi demanat a Sánchez durant mesos, Alberto Núñez Feijóo s'ha mostrat satisfet amb l'anunci de convocatòria d'eleccions . El líder dels populars creu que ha arribat el moment de convertir-se en el nou president del govern espanyol:

Per fi Espanya dirà el que pensa, per fi parlarà la majoria, per fi decidiran els espanyols.

En una compareixença des de la seu del PP, Feijóo s'ha erigit com l'encarregat de " tancar aquest temps i obrir-ne un altre de millor ". En aquest sentit, ha considerat que el de Sánchez era un "projecte d'ambició personalista" i a partir d'ara començarà "un projecte de país".

En una entrevista televisiva el líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal , ha demanat "no confiar en les enquestes" i ha vaticinat que els resultats seran " molt incerts ". Ha qualificat Sánchez de " candidat del Marroc ", ha dit que en les eleccions es votarà amb " Ceuta envaïda " i ha assegurat que coincideix amb el PP que Espanya "necessita un canvi radical ".

Des de Sumar han assegurat que estan llestos per afrontar les generals malgrat que estan en transició cap a la nova marca electoral Front Ampli, que encara no té candidat després de la renúncia de Yolanda Díaz .

L'espai pretén situar l'habitatge com a "assumpte central d'aquest moment polític" i diu que en els pròxims dies comunicarà "la marca electoral i la candidatura, així com les aliances, a mesura que es vagin produint, fins a culminar en un gran acte el 17 d'octubre".

Des de Junts, conscients que han contribuït a aquest avançament electoral, han acusat Pedro Sánchez d'haver utilitzat "el dolor i el patiment de molta gent" en la qüestió de l'habitatge "per interessos electorals".

La cap de files de Junts al Congrés, Miriam Nogueras , li ha retret que hauria d'haver convocat eleccions "molt abans" i que ha volgut tapar amb aquesta convocatòria "la seva incapacitat de governar perquè no té majoria, el seu fracàs en les polítiques migratòries i els casos de corrupció que l'envolten".

Des de la seu d' Esquerra , la secretària general del partit, Elisenda Alamany , ha assegurat que Gabriel Rufián és el millor candidat per encapçalar la seva llista. Fonts properes a Rufián asseguren que està valorant si serà el candidat de la formació. Poc abans el líder d'ERC, Oriol Junqueras , ha fet una publicació a X assegurant que els republicans estan preparats per afrontar la campanya. "Preparats per defensar Catalunya i trencar-nos la cara per millorar la vida de la gent", ha dit.

A lo largo de su carrera política, Sánchez se ha ganado la reputación de ser un escapista político capaz de ganar elecciones que parecía destinado a perder

Este próximo 29 de noviembre, los españoles están llamados a la urnas para votar en unas elecciones generales que Pedro Sánchez adelantó este lunes, aproximadamente ocho meses antes de lo previsto. En las últimas semanas, los españoles han efectuado protestas en diversas ciudades para exigir soluciones al Gobierno sobre la arraigada crisis habitacional , en medio de la indignación por el desahucio de la anciana Maricarmen .

El Gobierno de Sánchez sufrió una dura derrota legislativa la semana pasada, cuando el Congreso rechazó los decretos de urgencia presentados por su gobierno para hacer frente a los desahucios y la especulación inmobiliaria. Sánchez, de 54 años, es presidente del gobierno español desde 2018, lo que lo convierte en uno de los líderes europeos que más tiempo lleva en el cargo.

Los sondeos dejan entrever que el Partido Popular y Vox podrían, juntos, ganar suficiente apoyo para desalojar a Sánchez de la Moncloa. Mientras, la extrema izquierda sigue descabezada y en las últimas horas, la ejecutiva de Comuns se ha mostrado este lunes mayoritariamente favorable a que la ex alcaldesa de Barcelona Ada Colau sea la cabeza de cartel de Frente Amplio.

El Consejo de Ministros ha aprobado nuevamente los dos reales decretos sobre vivienda "con algunas incorporaciones", que cayeron en el Congreso el viernes pasado. En concreto, se trata de 21 medidas que incluye novedades sobre todo en el ámbito para facilitar el acceso a la compra. Sánchez ha anunciado una línea de financiación dotada con 10.000 millones de euros para la concesión de préstamos de hasta 50.000 euros sin intereses para quienes quieren adquirir su primera vivienda porque "ahorrar para la hipoteca se ha vuelto el mayor obstáculo para la emancipación", ha dicho el presidente de Gobierno.

sources.body:
El temporal de lluvias continúa azotando Cataluña, donde este martes se repiten los cortes en carreteras e incidencias ferroviarias y se busca a dos personas desaparecidas . Se trata de un hombre en Pineda del Mar, Barcelona, al que dos personas vieron cómo era arrastrado por el agua; y un menor en Granollers, cuya desaparición no estaría en principio vinculada a las precipitaciones, pero sí estarían dificultando su búsqueda. El fin de semana dejó, a su vez, dos muertes en Tordera y en Montornès del Vallès .

En cuanto a las incidencias, ocho carreteras siguen afectadas : dos de ellas están cortadas (la C-1415a, en Castellar del Vallès, y la C-352, en el túnel entre les Franqueses del Vallès y Canovelles); y se ha suspendido el tráfico en algunos carriles de la C-31, en Sant Adrià del Besòs, con el acceso a la Ronda Litoral; en la C-35, en Vidreres; la C-59, en Bigues i Riells; la GI-682, entre Tossa de Mar y Sant Feliu de Guíxols, y en esta misma carretera en Blanes, y la N-150, en Terrassa.

Las principales vías de acceso a Barcelona han registrado retenciones de varios kilómetros desde primera hora de esta mañana, especialmente, la B-10 (Ronda Litoral) y la B-20 (Ronda de Dalt). Todo ello coincide con afectaciones en Rodalies en casi todas las líneas salvo en la R2, la R2Sud R15, R16, RT1, RL3 y RL4.

En la R2 Nord se ha dispuesto un servicio alternativo por carretera entre Granollers Centre y Sant Celoni, mientras que el tramo Granollers Centre-Aeroport no funciona. En R1, R3, R4, R13, R14, R17 y RT2 hay servicios alternativos en varios puntos y las líneas R7 y R8 continúan sin servicio ferroviario, por lo que Renfe recomienda a los estudiantes universitarios que utilicen la línea de bus exprés e3, entre Barcelona, Cerdanyola del Vallès y la Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB), Bellaterra. En el Metro de Barcelona se ha normalizado este lunes por la noche tras las incidencias por las lluvias, excepto la estación Liceu de la L3.

Sobre las previsiones, esta jornada las lluvias podrán alcanzar más de 40 litros por metro cuadrado en 30 minutos en zonas de Cataluña como el litoral de Barcelona y litoral sur de Girona.

Mientras el temporal se extiende a toda España. Trece comunidades autónomas están este martes bajo aviso por lluvias y tormentas, seis de ellas en nivel naranja (peligro importante), por fuertes precipitaciones.

Se encuentran en nivel naranja de riesgo , además de Cataluña, las siguientes comunidades: Aragón, Asturias, Castilla-La Mancha, Extremadura y Galicia, de acuerdo a las predicciones de la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet). En aviso amarillo por lluvia, están: Andalucía, Castilla y León, Comunidad de Madrid, Comunidad Foral de Navarra, La Rioja, Comunitat Valenciana y Canarias.

Las precipitaciones podrán superar más 30 litros por metro cuadrado en una hora en zonas del nordeste; en concreto en el Pirineo oscense y centro de Huesca, y también en el Pirineo de Lleida. Asimismo, se superarán esos niveles de lluvias en los montes del norte y Anchuras, Ciudad Real, y también en los montes de Toledo. Igualmente en Villuercas y Montánchez, Cáceres, y en la Siberia extremeña; además, en el noroeste peninsular en la suroccidental asturiana; y en el interior de A Coruña, Galicia, y centro de Lugo y zona de la montaña.

EL PERIÓDICO ofrece en este directo la última hora del tráfico y la movilidad en Catalunya , con especial atención a las graves afectaciones provocadas por el episodio de lluvias del fin de semana. Sigue en tiempo real las retenciones, carreteras cortadas, desprendimientos, inundaciones e incidencias que están complicando los desplazamientos, especialmente en Barcelona y su área metropolitana.

El directo recoge también las importantes afectaciones en Rodalies y otros servicios de transporte público , así como los cambios en el servicio, las líneas afectadas y las alternativas para los viajeros. Toda la información sobre el estado de las carreteras y del transporte público, además de los avisos y recomendaciones que puedan condicionar la movilidad durante la jornada.

Rodalies mantiene este mediodía afectaciones en varias líneas por los efectos del temporal de lluvias .

La R1 circula entre L’Hospitalet y Arenys de Mar con demoras medias de 20 minutos , mientras que el tramo Arenys-Maçanet funciona con autobuses.

También hay servicios alternativos por carretera en tramos de la R2 Nord, R3, R4, R8, R11, RG1, R13, R14, RL4, RT1, R17 y RT2 .

La situación más restrictiva se mantiene en la R7, sin servicio ferroviario en todo su recorrido , para la que se recomienda utilizar el bus exprés e3 entre Barcelona, Cerdanyola y la UAB.

FGC, por su parte, funciona con normalidad.

Protecció Civil pide evitar zonas inundables y no atravesar riadas, pasos bajos o vados ante la posibilidad de crecidas repentinas. Los Agents Rurals mantienen el seguimiento de ríos, rieras y torrentes y han revisado y cerrado accesos en puntos donde se ha detectado riesgo.

La recomendación llega en una jornada en la que la red de carreteras y el transporte público todavía están recuperándose de las afectaciones de los últimos días y ante la previsión de nuevas lluvias esta tarde.

La red viaria todavía arrastra las consecuencias de los episodios de lluvia de los últimos días. Continúan cortadas la C-1415a, en el puente de la Roca del Vallès, y la C-352, en el túnel entre les Franqueses del Vallès y Canovelles .

Además, hay afectaciones en la GI-682 entre Tossa de Mar y Sant Feliu de Guíxols , por desprendimientos, y en Blanes , por inundaciones. Trànsit recomienda extremar la precaución y respetar la señalización, especialmente ante la previsión de nuevas precipitaciones.

Protecció Civil tiene activado el plan INUNCAT en fase de emergencia ante la previsión de nuevas lluvias intensas este martes. El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya alerta de precipitaciones que pueden ser torrenciales, con más de 40 l/m² en 30 minutos en algunos puntos.

A partir del mediodía, el episodio puede afectar especialmente al Prepirineo de Lleida, las Terres de l’Ebre y el Camp de Tarragona. Por la tarde, y especialmente a última hora y por la noche, la lluvia se desplazará hacia el litoral y prelitoral, desde el Baix Penedès hasta el Baix Empordà. La previsión puede complicar de nuevo los desplazamientos.

La circulación de los autobuses de TMB de las líneas 62, 76 y 183 ya se ha restablecido en la avenida dels Rasos de Peguera . También vuelven a estar operativas las paradas 1626, 2604 y 2605 .

sources.body: L’Ajuntament de Barcelona impulsarà una modificació de les ordenances fiscals per apujar l’IBI fins al 150 % als pisos turístics . Ho ha dit a Catalunya Ràdio el tinent d’alcaldia d’Economia, Jordi Valls, que ha explicat que portaran la mesura en una comissió d’economia extraordinària aquesta mateixa setmana, o a principis de la vinent. El govern Collboni ho podrà fer un cop la Diputació Permanent aprovi els decrets d’habitatge que el Congrés dels Diputats va tombar divendres , que permeten als consistoris augmentar la fiscalitat als habitatges que es destinen a l’ ús turístic . També et pot interessar Pedro Sánchez troba una via alternativa per aprovar els decrets d’habitatge tombats pel Congrés Marina Segura i Vidal 1 minut de lectura Divendres, l’alcalde Collboni va donar per perduda aquesta possibilitat , després que Junts, el PP i Vox votessin en contra dels decrets. Ara, en canvi, l’escenari és un altre. Amb el Congrés dissolt per la convocatòria d’eleccions , el president, Pedro Sánchez, durà a votació de nou els decrets al Consell de Ministres aquest mateix dimarts perquè, després, els aprovi la Diputació Permanent, que assumeix les funcions de la cambra baixa en períodes electorals i que és de majoria progressista . Màxima fiscalitat als propietaris de més de quatre pisos El tinent Valls ha defensat que aquesta mesura ha de servir per desincentivar els pisos turístics mentre no s’apliqui la prohibició total , prevista per al 2028 . En concret, la normativa preveu un recàrrec de fins al 50 % per als titulars d’un pis turístic; de fins al 100 % per als que en tenen entre dos i quatre; i fins al 150 % quan el titular és propietari de quatre o més habitatges destinats a aquest ús. Segons va dir l’alcalde, els càlculs municipals indiquen que amb aquest augment de l’impost es podrien recaptar uns 7 M€ cada any, que es destinarien a la promoció d’habitatge protegit a Barcelona. També et pot interessar Mobilització massiva a Barcelona pel dret a l’habitatge: “Volem que la vaga sigui un èxit” Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura Els comuns demanen celeritat Collboni té garantit el suport del Grup Municipal de BComú, que ha demanat a l’acalde que porti a aprovació la mesura de manera urgent , perquè entri en vigor el gener del 2027. “Demanem a l’alcalde que sigui coherent . Per una vegada, que no s’amagui sota la retòrica”, ha exigit la regidora Carol Recio. El govern municipal també tindrà el sí dels regidors republicans perquè, de fet, Sánchez va incloure aquesta mesura en els decrets a petició d’ Esquerra Republicana . El grup parlamentari d’ @Esquerra_ERC al Congrés va pactar amb el PSOE incloure als decrets d’habitatge la possibilitat d’apujar l’IBI als pisos turístics.
